title: Traffic split inconsistency from proxy header duplication blocked canary progression
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a staged model rollout we observed that the canary did not receive its intended proportion of traffic despite route configuration showing correct weights. Root cause analysis identified a proxy-layer behavior that duplicated our routing header (X-Redwood-Route) for a subset of requests, causing the route-translator to see conflicting headers and fall back to a legacy routing path. This led to a persistent ~12% under-allocation of canary traffic for ~3 hours, delaying rollout decisions and causing elevated tail latency on the legacy model. Impact: internal customer-facing features experienced slight latency regressions; no data exfiltration or incorrect model outputs were observed.

root_cause: A proxy sidecar change intended for extended debug logging appended a second X-Redwood-Route header for requests that matched an internal healthprobe path. The route-translator component treats multiple routing headers as a conflict and applies an older compatibility path which ignores the latest route weights. The combination of duplicated headers and route-translator conflict resolution resulted in systematic under-routing to the canary variant.
mitigations: Added temporary edge proxy filter to drop duplicate X-Redwood-Route headers (applied 2026-03-01 10:05)
Paused ongoing rollouts automatically via rollout-controller when observed traffic deviates >7% from expected (temporary guard)
Applied traffic verification alert (dashboard) to detect routing header divergence and trigger pager on future incidents
